failures.title: Land Rover AJ20D6 Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: EGR Cooler and Cooling System Leaks
items.whatHappens: Early production runs of the AJ20D6 have shown a susceptibility to micro-cracking in the EGR cooler core. This allows exhaust gases to pressurise the cooling system, leading to unexplained coolant loss, expansion tank swelling, and potential mixing of coolant with soot. If ignored, this can lead to localized overheating and cylinder head warpage.
items.repairVsReplace: If caught early, replacing the EGR cooler and associated hoses is a straightforward repair. However, if overheating has occurred and the cylinder head is compromised, a full Land Rover AJ20D6 engine replacement is the only guaranteed fix.

items.title: Mild-Hybrid (MHEV) Electrical Gremlins
items.whatHappens: The 48-volt mild-hybrid system relies on a belt-integrated starter generator (BISG) and associated power inverters. Early software calibration issues or inverter faults can trigger drivetrain malfunction warnings, forcing the vehicle into limp mode or preventing the engine from restarting after an auto-stop event.
items.repairVsReplace: Most MHEV issues are resolved with JLR software updates or targeted component replacement. However, if the BISG or inverter failure is severe and integrated deeply with the engine assembly, a full unit swap may be required, particularly if the vehicle is out of warranty.

failures.goodYearsLine: As a very recent architecture (2020+), the AJ20D6 has largely avoided the catastrophic bottom-end bearing failures that plagued older V6 diesels like the 306DT. Most documented issues are manageable peripheral component or software updates, making it one of the most robust modern Land Rover diesels to date .

variants.title: How to Confirm You Have the AJ20D6
variants.intro: As a Specific page type with no distinct sub-codes listed in the inventory, this section focuses on accurate identification and avoiding common, costly misidentifications. The AJ20D6 engine code is stamped on a machined pad on the cylinder block and is also recorded on your vehicle’s V5C registration document under "Engine Number". Owners and breakers frequently confuse the AJ20D6 with its predecessors, the 306DT or the 30DDTX. While all three are 3.0-litre Land Rover diesels, the AJ20D6 is a fundamentally different architecture: it is a true inline-6 featuring a 48-volt mild-hybrid (MHEV) system, a different block casting, and a completely revised engine management and wiring layout. The older 306DT is a 60-degree V6 with no hybrid integration, and the 30DDTX is a transitional design. Fitting a 306DT or 30DDTX wiring harness, ECU, or ancillary components to an AJ20D6 host will result in a non-running vehicle and significant wasted expenditure.

relatives.description: The - the outgoing 3.0-litre V6 diesel that the AJ20D6 replaced in Land Rover's lineup, which carried a known risk of catastrophic crankshaft bearing failure that the modern inline-six architecture was specifically designed to eliminate.

The - the transitional 3.0-litre V6 diesel that bridged the gap between the older Lion V6 architecture and the modern Ingenium inline-six, sharing similar emissions complexities but lacking the mild-hybrid integration.

The - the 3.0-litre mild-hybrid petrol inline-six that shares the exact same foundational Ingenium block architecture, 48-volt electrical system, and chassis mounting points, but features a different internal configuration and fuel delivery system.

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement AJ20D6 - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: A used Land Rover AJ20D6 engine for sale can be a viable option for rolling repairs, provided the seller can supply comprehensive Land Rover service records and confirmation that all early EGR cooler and MHEV software recalls have been actioned. Without this history, you risk inheriting early teething issues that could escalate quickly. Learn more about used engines.

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: For most modern Land Rover owners, a reconditioned AJ20D6 is the optimal choice. A proper recon will proactively address the engine’s known weaknesses by fitting updated EGR cooler revisions, ensuring the 48V mild-hybrid components are fully tested and calibrated to the latest software, and replacing all perishable seals, delivering near-new reliability for the future. Explore reconditioned engine options.

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: A full rebuild is justified for high-mileage, heavily used Defender or Discovery examples where the engine is being stripped to the bare block. This allows for comprehensive cleaning, seal replacement, and verification of the MHEV integration points, ensuring the engine matches the pristine specification of the host chassis. View rebuilt engine services.

items.answer: The most documented failures on the AJ20D6 relate to the EGR cooler and the 48-volt mild-hybrid (MHEV) system. items.question: Which Land Rover models use the AJ20D6 engine?
items.answer: The AJ20D6 engine was introduced in 2020 and is fitted to the latest generation of Land Rover's core models, including the Defender (L663), Range Rover (L460), and Discovery (L462). It serves as the flagship diesel powerplant, offered in D250, D300, and D350 power outputs. It replaced the older 306DT and 30DDTX V6 architectures across the entire modern lineup.

items.question: Should I buy a used or reconditioned AJ20D6 engine?
items.answer: For a modern Land Rover, a reconditioned AJ20D6 is strongly recommended over a used unit. Used engines may carry unresolved early-production EGR cooler issues or outdated MHEV software calibrations. A proper reconditioned build proactively installs updated EGR cooler revisions, ensures the 48V mild-hybrid components are fully tested, and applies the latest ECU software. Reconditioned units also include comprehensive pressure testing to guarantee long-term reliability.

items.question: How do I know if my car has the AJ20D6 engine?
items.answer: You can confirm your engine code by checking the V5C registration document under the "Engine Number" field or by locating the code stamped on the cylinder block. The AJ20D6 is a 3.0-litre inline-6, physically distinct from the older 306DT or 30DDTX, which are 60-degree V6 configurations. It is also easily identified by the presence of the 48-volt mild-hybrid (MHEV) belt-integrated starter generator (BISG) and associated electrical architecture. Fitting an older V6 wiring harness or ECU to an AJ20D6 host will result in a non-running vehicle.
